players.name: DK Metcalf
players.note: Pittsburgh's offense was a mediocre 15th in scoring and 16th in ANY/A in 2025, and Aaron Rodgers gives solid but age-42 QB play now facing real target competition from newly added Michael Pittman Jr.; a lingering Aug 2026 ankle/undisclosed injury (on top of a 2025 marred by suspension, an ankle injury, and a hospitalization scare) trims durability below the default even though he says he'll be ready for Week 1, but his league-leading career red-zone target volume keeps some touchdown-driven upside alive.

players.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
players.note: Shares the backfield with Henderson on a still-unproven-but-improving line, capping his floor as a pure committee back; Henderson's undiagnosed right leg/ankle injury and Stevenson's healthiest camp in years give him a real (not certain) path to more work, while a three-year pattern of ankle/foot issues (season-ending IR in 2023) keeps his games projection short of a true workhorse number.

players.name: Dak Prescott
players.note: Cowboys finished 7th in scoring in 2025 with an unchanged offense returning intact behind an elite Lamb/Pickens WR duo, but the 2024 season-ending hamstring surgery (missed 9 games) and a prior 2020 season-ender temper durability despite a fully healthy, all-17-games 2025 season; at 33 in a settled role there's little room above the projection.

players.name: Chuba Hubbard
players.note: Bottom-10 Carolina offense with both starting tackles and both guards banged up ahead of a healthy, ascending Jonathon Brooks who threatens the touch share; hamstring kept him out the back half of preseason (targeting Week 1) after a Week 4 knee injury cost him his starting role for stretches of 2025.

players.name: Tony Pollard
players.note: Firmly RB1 in TN but stuck behind a bottom-5 run-blocking line (30th in rush yards, 4.2 YPC) on a bottom-half offense; remarkably durable (17, 16, 17 games last three years) but at 29 with only 5 TDs on 1,082 yards there's no touchdown role or age-driven upside to unlock.

players.name: RJ Harvey
players.note: Elite Denver OL (PFF's #1 unit for 2026) but a real committee with Dobbins capping his floor, and offense finished only 14th in scoring in 2025; upside is real since Dobbins (27, coming off a Lisfranc) is the injury-prone bell cow ahead of him and Harvey already showed a 12-TD role as a rookie.

players.name: Justin Herbert
players.note: Offense was 20th in scoring in 2025 and the McDaniel hire is unproven in LA; protection is the bigger worry with 60 sacks allowed last year and starting center Biadasz likely out for the season after an August 2026 knee injury in camp.

players.name: Courtland Sutton
players.note: Denver's offense was middling (14th, 23.6 ppg) in 2025, and the Waddle trade adds a clear WR1-caliber target hog ahead of Sutton on a room that already had Franklin and Mims, so his target share shrinks rather than grows at 30.

players.name: Rico Dowdle
players.note: Signed in to split the backfield with Warren (and Johnson in the mix) behind a middling line, and he's already nursing a nagging injury that kept him out of a preseason game; only gets a real bump if Warren's snaps come loose.

players.name: Michael Wilson
players.note: Cardinals released Kyler Murray in March 2026, so Jacoby Brissett (with rookie Carson Beck behind him) is the QB now, a real downgrade that caps the passing game, and Wilson still splits targets with Marvin Harrison Jr. and Trey McBride despite his 1,006-yard 2025 breakout.

players.name: J.K. Dobbins
players.note: Elite Broncos O-line is offset by a real three-way committee (Coleman impressing, Harvey on passing downs), and Dobbins already left an Aug 2026 camp practice with a soft-tissue injury on top of Achilles (2023), MCL (2024), and foot surgery (2025) the last three years.

players.name: Jordyn Tyson
players.note: 8th overall pick suffered a hamstring strain in August (his 4th in 4 years) and is expected out ~8 weeks with a week-5 return the earliest realistic case; QB Tyler Shough is unproven (9 career starts) but Kellen Moore's offense is genuinely hard to peg either way, and he'll compete with Chris Olave for targets once back, so he's a clear WR2-in-waiting with real upside if the hamstring holds up.

players.name: Makai Lemon
players.note: AJ Brown's trade to NE opens a real WR2 role opposite DeVonta Smith with Hurts throwing, but a recurring hamstring issue (out since Aug 3, only just back to full practice Aug 24) and zero NFL track record temper the games projection for a rookie first-rounder.

players.name: George Kittle
players.note: Purdy is solid but unspectacular and now splits red-zone/perimeter looks with newly-signed Mike Evans, capping Kittle's ceiling; recovering from a January Achilles tear on top of hamstring absences in both 2024 and 2025 (off PUP, targeting Week 1 but recurrence/management risk is real) is the whole story here.

players.name: Jonathon Brooks
players.note: Fully cleared and taking full-speed camp reps, but stuck behind entrenched starter Hubbard on a bottom-tier offense, and two ACL tears on the same knee in two years keep the injury risk real even with no current designation.

players.name: Jaxson Dart
players.note: Took over as Giants QB1 mid-2025 on a bottom-half offense with a shaky line; Nabers is a true WR1 but is still working back from an October ACL/meniscus repair with no set return date, and Dart's aggressive rushing style already cost him two games to a concussion as a rookie. Full-time job, second-year jump, and rushing TD equity give real ceiling above the projection.

players.name: Dalton Kincaid
players.note: Josh Allen elevates him but DJ Moore's arrival plus Shakir and Coleman make targets crowded, and he's missed 4-5 games in each of the last two seasons (played through a torn PCL in 2025, new knee scare at Aug 2026 camp) with the team openly discussing load management.

players.name: Kyle Monangai
players.note: Top-10 Ben Johnson offense behind a top-5 line, but he's RB2 to Swift and is week-to-week with a hyperextended knee that puts the Sept 13 opener in question; his rookie-year breakout as CHI's leading rusher and Swift's own injury history keep real upside once healthy.

players.name: Travis Kelce
players.note: Confirmed playing (re-signed, TE1 on 2026 depth chart) despite retirement chatter, but a bottom-half Chiefs offense (22nd PPG in 2025) with Mahomes still working back from a late-season knee injury caps the ceiling, and Kelce has slid to a secondary read (18% first-read target share) behind Rashee Rice; at 36 he's durable historically but has no growth path left.

players.name: Blake Corum
players.note: Firmly RB2 behind Kyren Williams in a good Stafford-led offense, but Kyren has a multi-year history of high-ankle sprains (missed time in 2022, 2023, 2024), so Corum's touches could spike fast if that recurs; TD work still concentrated with Kyren (13 TD vs Corum's 6 in 2025).

players.name: Chris Godwin
players.note: Evans' departure leaves Godwin as clear WR2 behind Egbuka with less target competition, but back-to-back years of major injuries (2024 ankle dislocation/surgery, 2025 fibula issue plus PUP stint) make durability the dominant risk at 30.

players.name: Alec Pierce
players.note: Colts' 2025 offense was one of the league's best behind Jones and Taylor, but Pierce had left-ankle cleanup surgery in March after playing hurt in 2024-25 and is on Active/PUP with the team itself signaling he'll miss the start of 2026, while Downs and Warren eat into his target share even once he's back.

players.name: Matthew Stafford
players.note: Coming off an MVP-level 2025 with Nacua and Adams both healthy and a competent if unspectacular line, but the aggravated back disc that wiped out his 2025 camp is a real recurring issue at 38, and he's already playing at his ceiling with no growth left to unlock.

players.name: Trevor Lawrence
players.note: Played all 17 games in a career-best 2025 under Liam Coen, but the 2024 season-ending concussion/shoulder injury and camp-week OL health scares keep durability a real question; Brian Thomas Jr. and Travis Hunter give him a genuinely strong receiver duo even with offense quality unproven beyond passing-volume stats.

players.name: Jake Ferguson
players.note: Dak Prescott is a plus QB but Lamb and Pickens soak up the target share and red-zone looks ahead of him, capping how much of the passing game reaches the TE; coming off a healthy 17-game, 8-TD 2025 but with a concussion and MCL sprain the year before, so durability is a real if modest question.
